newsitem.title: JAPAN: TIFFE euroyen flat before BOJ news conference.
newsitem.headline: TIFFE euroyen flat before BOJ news conference.

text.p: Key December three-month euroyen interest rate futures were unchanged at Wednesday midday after subdued trade amid a lack of fresh factors.
Traders said they were taking a wait-and-see attitude ahead of Bank of Japan (BOJ) governor Yasuo Matsushita's regular news conference scheduled at 3 p.m. (0600 GMT).

"The December was caught in a narrow band. It failed to rally as cash money market rates were under upward pressure. But price firmness in Japanese government bond (JGB) futures underpinned the downside," said a city bank dealer.
The December stood at 99.08, unchanged from Tuesday close.
It moved between 99.07 and 99.09 after opening at 99.09. Turnover was 10,137 contracts.
In the interbank market, the key overnight call rate fell to 0.48 percent by midday from Tuesday's 0.53 percent.

The rate's fall was attributed to the BOJ's keeping extra accommodative credit stance since Friday last week. The bank left a surplus of an estimated 210 billion yen by draining 400 billion yen from the market through its Wednesday operation.
"The BOJ's leaving a surplus of some 200 billion yen for the last couple of days affected the market eventually," said another city bank dealer.

A long-term credit bank dealer said one factor easing the key rate on Wednesday was that some city banks had raised one- to two-week funds at higher rates on Tuesday to cover Japan's Golden Week holidays, a peak in seasonal fund demand.
But longer-term money market rates were firmly underpinned due to a lack of funds from investors, traders said.
"Investors refrained from buying three-month certificates of deposit (CD) recently due to vague fears of higher interest rates in and after July," said another bank dealer.
The key three-month CDs were offered at 0.56 percent this morning, unchanged from Tuesday's issued rate.
